items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: So I didn't know anything about Dizzy, you know. And all I knew that all the trumpet players tried to play like Roy. Everybody but Dizzy.

ctx.x: Did this start happening when you were (inaudible) little children?

Yes. And I guess I'm really getting ahead of my story, but you know my mother used to have a choir in Montgomery, and I would have to go to choir practice with her. And I used to sit in the balcony of this empty church while they were practicing, you know, rehearsing, on stage. And I used to hear all kind of sounds. They would sing certain kind of tunes, or songs, and I would sing just something contrapuntal to that, by myself. And I would hear different voices and I would go on a tangent from where they were…

And I just always heard like this, you know. So as I say, it was just a gift, I guess, you know. But coming back to Charlie Christian, I heard Dizzy say -- Dizzy's the only one who really tells the truth about -- I don't say tell the truth. Who really is aware what happened. I never tried
